questions.stem_text: Seven people standing silently while waiting for a bus at a bus stop is an example of which of the following?
questions.answer_explanation: Correct option: C - An aggregate

questions.stem_text: Chodorow (1978) argued that gender socialization occurred through:

options.A: both boys and girls being closely attached to their mothers, but then boys breaking away
options.B: girls being attached to their mothers but then breaking away
options.C: boys being attached to their fathers and girls to their mothers
options.D: both boys and girls being closely attached to their fathers, but girls breaking away

questions.answer_explanation: Correct option: A - both boys and girls being closely attached to their mothers, but then boys breaking away

questions.stem_text: The media-themes model of media influence claims that:

options.A: audiences selectively interpret what they want to hear
options.B: content analysis is the best way to identify the themes covered by the media
options.C: audiences passively absorb whatever messages they are given
options.D: social interaction reinforces the ideas and images that audiences select

questions.answer_explanation: Correct option: D - social interaction reinforces the ideas and images that audiences select

questions.stem_text: A moral panic occurs when:

options.A: the media exaggerate reports of deviant groups, generating hostile reactions
options.B: children watch violent or sexually explicit films and then copy the behaviour
options.C: audiences challenge the ethnic stereotypes represented by the media
options.D: elitists express concern with the Americanization of culture

questions.answer_explanation: Correct option: A - the media exaggerate reports of deviant groups, generating hostile reactions

questions.stem_text: Someone who gains a higher (or lower) social position than he or she was born into has experienced
questions.answer_explanation: Correct option: C - vertical mobility

questions.stem_text: The capitalist world economy is what Wallerstein (1974) would call a 'world system'. This term refers to:

options.A: a means of transporting money between different areas of a country
options.B: an empire with a bureaucratic administration but no political centre
options.C: an awareness of risks and dangers that affect the environment as a whole
options.D: a unit with a division of labour that extends across ethnic and cultural groups

questions.answer_explanation: Correct option: D - a unit with a division of labour that extends across ethnic and cultural groups

questions.stem_text: In Symbolic Interactionist theory, Mead defined the 'generalized other' as:

options.A: the group of structural theories of society that he was reacting against
options.B: the overall impression of ourselves that we try to give off to others
options.C: a significant figure in early childhood who teaches us the general values of society
options.D: an image of how people in the wider society might perceive our behaviour

questions.answer_explanation: Correct option: D - an image of how people in the wider society might perceive our behaviour

questions.stem_text: In the traditional hierarchy of status and precedence, which of these members of the upper class are in the right order (from highest to lowest status)?

options.A: Prime Minister, Archbishop of York, Viscounts of England
options.B: Marquesses of England, Earls of Great Britain, King's Brothers
options.C: Esquires, Serjeants of Law, Dukes' Eldest Sons
options.D: King's Grandsons, Lord High Treasurer, Companions of the Bath

questions.answer_explanation: Correct option: D - King's Grandsons, Lord High Treasurer, Companions of the Bath

questions.stem_text: Marx (1844) claimed that capitalism had alienated workers from:

options.C: each other and humanity in general

questions.answer_explanation: Correct option: D - all of the above

questions.stem_text: According to Davis (1995), women may seek cosmetic surgery because:

options.A: they have a deep-rooted sense of ineffectiveness and are striving for control
options.B: they are in pursuit of the 'perfect' body, fuelled by images of beauty
options.C: they perceive a part of their body as stigmatizing, in relation to a cultural ideal
options.D: their male partners pressurize them to look like supermodels

questions.answer_explanation: Correct option: C - they perceive a part of their body as stigmatizing, in relation to a cultural ideal

questions.stem_text: Which of the following was not part of Weber's ideal type of bureaucracy?
questions.answer_explanation: Correct option: B - extensive paperwork

questions.stem_text: Economic aid has largely failed to promote modernization in the developing countries because:

options.A: there are no clearly defined projects into which the money can be directed
options.B: the United Nations has refused to call on rich countries to provide it
options.C: debt repayments with interest can be greater than the amount of money received
options.D: debt repayments with interest can be greater than the amount of money received

questions.answer_explanation: Correct option: C - debt repayments with interest can be greater than the amount of money received

questions.stem_text: Marriage appears to be in decline because:

options.A: the proportion of people living alone has fallen to 29\%
options.B: many people are cohabiting in long term relationships
options.C: the upward curve of remarriages compensates for the drop in first marriages

questions.answer_explanation: Correct option: B - many people are cohabiting in long term relationships

questions.stem_text: Weber (1919) said that the state's monopoly of the use of force was legitimated by:
questions.answer_explanation: Correct option: B - rational-legal authority

questions.stem_text: World-affirming religions:

options.A: embrace conventional cultural values but offer new means of achieving them
options.B: react against the loss of any meaningful religious content in the teachings of churches
options.C: adopt an attitude of mild disapproval towards mainstream social values
options.D: reject both the goals and means of conventional society and provide utopian alternatives

questions.answer_explanation: Correct option: A - embrace conventional cultural values but offer new means of achieving them

questions.stem_text: Disciplinary power was exercised in the 19th century factories by:

options.A: the use of corporal punishment by employers
options.B: excluding women from participating in waged labour
options.C: punctuality, uninterrupted work and the threat of dismissal

questions.answer_explanation: Correct option: C - punctuality, uninterrupted work and the threat of dismissal

questions.stem_text: Herberg's (1955) study of religion in America suggested that:

options.A: ethnic minorities practised religion to achieve social acceptance in the culture
options.B: mainstream faiths were becoming increasingly identified with national identity
options.C: the moral teachings of the main religions were becoming relatively similar

questions.answer_explanation: Correct option: D - all of the above

questions.stem_text: Becker proclaimed that cannabis use was:

options.A: increasing throughout all sections of youth in the 1970s
options.B: learned gradually through the social processes of a deviant career
options.C: a dangerous pastime that young people should not be allowed to pursue
options.D: not as enjoyable as other sociologists had suggested

questions.answer_explanation: Correct option: B - learned gradually through the social processes of a deviant career

questions.stem_text: The correct answer to 'Scientific management involved:' is 'the subdivision of labour into small tasks'.
questions.answer_explanation: Actual answer is 'all of the above'.

questions.stem_text: The correct answer to 'The 1944 Education Act provided:' is 'free secondary education for all'.
questions.answer_explanation: Matches the MMLU answer key.
